- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to underpredict sharp upward moves; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% for the first 5–7 days after sentiment spike.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0) and price is trending up, model often overestimates continuation; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.
- After a strong price spike (≥1.5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1.5–2.0% above peak for 3–7 days.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.2) and price is volatile, model exhibits mean reversion bias; add 0.3–0.8% upward bias to forecast for 5–10 days to avoid premature correction.
- If true outcome shows early sharp decline after a peak, model often lags by 1–3 days; shift forecast downward by 0.5–1.0% for next 2–4 days if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates downward trends after sentiment turns negative; add 0.5–1.5% downward bias for first 5 days if sentiment drops below 0.1.
